questions.prompt: You run PCA on X and on X + 1000 and get very different first components. What went wrong?
options: Nothing, because PCA depends on location
The data wasn't centered before the eigendecomposition or SVD
You divided by n instead of n − 1
You used eigh instead of eig
questions.explanation: PCA describes variation around the mean. Without centering, the first direction mostly points toward the mean, which moves when you shift the data.

questions.prompt: evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(C). Which is the first principal component?
questions.explanation: eigh returns eigenvalues in ascending order, and eigenvectors are columns. The largest-variance direction is the last column.

questions.prompt: For centered data with thin SVD Xc = U S Vᵀ, what are the explained variances?
questions.explanation: Xcᵀ Xc = V S² Vᵀ, so the covariance Xcᵀ Xc / (n − 1) has eigenvalues S² / (n − 1) and eigenvectors given by the rows of Vᵀ.

questions.prompt: eigh and SVD give components that match except some rows have opposite signs. Is that a bug?
options: No, v and −v are equally valid. Apply a sign convention to make outputs deterministic
Yes, the data must be standardized
questions.explanation: An eigenvector is defined only up to sign. Flip each component so a chosen entry (for example the largest-magnitude one) is positive, and both methods then agree.
